expectations.text: The answer identifies that M5Unified's internal I2C driver (M5.In_I2C) re-attaches pins 47/48 on its own transactions (e.g. during M5.update()), taking them away from Arduino Wire
expectations.evidence: answer.md:5-11 M5Unified owns bus, M5.update routes pins to its controller

expectations.text: The answer tells the user to access the BMI270 through M5.In_I2C (or M5Unified's own IMU access) instead of Wire on pins 47/48
The answer recommends the Bosch BMI270 legacy configuration (bmi270_legacy_*) for single/double tap and orientation, since the main config lacks them
The answer notes the SparkFun wrapper cannot load the legacy config, so the Bosch API bundled in it must be called directly
expectations.evidence: Says SparkFun cannot give legacy, but tells user to copy Bosch API files and remove SparkFun instead of using the bundled API (extra work, duplicate-symbol risk)

expectations.text: The answer provides code that maps features to an interrupt and reads events by polling the interrupt status register (and the tap status register for tap type)
